_comment: Single source of the deterministic rules of first-users-hunter: signal types and their maximum age, the classifier patterns, the activity gate, the score and the first-touch limits. Read by candidates.py, check_activity.py, score_people.py and verify_people.py. The model never scores. Override per project with <project>/first-users-hunter/criteria.json (keys merged over this file), or with recency_days and activity in config.json. Points are this stack's defaults, not figures from a study: change them, rerun, compare.

ask.label: asks for help, a recommendation or a tool for the task the product does

switch.label: leaves or replaces a tool or a way of working, asks for an alternative

complaint.label: complains about the status quo, a workaround or a competitor

question.label: asks a public question on the problem space, not yet a request for a tool

trigger.label: a dated public event that opens the need: company created, funding, a role hired, a launch

event.label: hosts or speaks at an event on the topic; the date is the event date and may be ahead

build.label: builds in public in an adjacent domain

listed.label: appears in a public list or directory: a seed, never a signal on its own

classifier._comment: First matching type wins, in this order. Case-insensitive regular expressions on title and text. The model may correct a type in people.jsonl; verify_people.py only checks it is a known type.

activity._comment: Gate: at least min_weighted_posts own public posts in the window, weighted by kind. LinkedIn gets a wider window because search engines index a fraction of its posts. Zero posts found means not proven, never inactive: a person not proven is left out of this run, not labelled dead.

touch_limits._comment: Characters unless words is set. Touch 1 never carries a link; touch 2 at most one. connection_note: LinkedIn cuts notes of free accounts at 200 characters. X replies: 280 characters.
